claim: Dania lists Cyber Security as its English full-degree offering for September 2027.
excerpt: Structured restatement: The full-degree catalogue welcomes international Cyber Security students from September 2027; its English-taught-programmes link leads to the Cyber Security programme. The catalogue also links Danish-taught programmes, summer schools and exchange activities; these are not additional English first-year degrees.

claim: Cyber Security is an English-taught 195 ECTS bachelor in Viborg beginning September 2027, with a six-month internship and an optional two-year AP exit.
excerpt: Structured restatement: Facts list English, Viborg, September 2027, 195 ECTS, 3¼ years and a six-month internship. The first 1½ years are shared; applicants apply to the bachelor and may exit after two years with an Academy Profession Degree in Operational Cyber Security. Semesters 1–3 cover business understanding, programming, computer architecture, communication, automation, data and network security, governance and software security. Semester 6 is a 30 ECTS internship; semester 7 includes a 10 ECTS bachelor project. Semester 4 Governance, Risk & Compliance is pending approval; specialisation and certification detail is due in November.

claim: Cyber Security requires English B and Mathematics B; quota 2 considers additional qualifications.
excerpt: Structured restatement: Specific entry requirements state English at Danish B level (210 hours of 60 minutes over the last three upper-secondary years) and mathematics at Danish B level (250 hours). Applicants applying by 15 March noon are assessed in quota 2, including additional qualifications. No weighting or complete scoring rubric is given.
interpretation: Keep the specific English B requirement. The same page separately mentions English C plus a test; it does not clearly establish whether that route also replaces the programme-specific English B condition. Applicants relying on it need clarification.

claim: Dania lists English tests with two-year validity but its English C plus test wording conflicts with the programme-specific English B requirement.
excerpt: Structured restatement: Under English requirements the page says English C plus an English test can satisfy the language requirement. Minimum scores listed are IELTS Academic or Indicator 6.5; TOEFL or TOEFL iBT Home Edition 4.5 or 94; Cambridge C1 Advanced 180; Cambridge C2 Proficiency 200; Oxford Online Placement Test C1 with at least 85 in each part, accepted only at Dania or an approved partner agency. Test validity is two years.
interpretation: The English C-plus-test paragraph does not clearly waive the specific English B condition on this programme. Preserve both statements without promising eligibility through a test alone; the TOEFL scales and test delivery should be confirmed before booking.

claim: Dania requires an application, school records, a school-signed verification form and photo ID; final documents follow admission-period instructions.
excerpt: Structured restatement: Apply through optagelse.dk from 1 February; the deadline for non-Danish upper-secondary qualifications is 15 March at noon. Upload diploma and transcript; if graduating after the deadline, upload the latest transcript by the application deadline and the final diploma as soon as received, following admission-period instructions. Translation is not required. Upload a signed and stamped upper-secondary verification form and photo ID. The exact September 2027 start date is not yet announced; orientation is in the preceding week.

claim: Dania exempts Danish and EU/EEA students and specified residence-permit holders from tuition; the fee payable by other students has not been announced.
excerpt: Structured restatement: No tuition for Danish students, EU/EEA students, permanent residents of Denmark, temporary residents whose permit allows permanent residence (mhp./mmf. varigt ophold), or temporary residents under §7(1–3), §8(1–2), §9(1) or §9c(1). All other students pay full tuition; the page says further non-EU fee details will follow. No 2027 amount or payment deadline is supplied.

claim: Dania describes small classes, industry contact and international-student and housing guidance at its Viborg campus.
excerpt: Structured restatement: Teaching uses smaller classes, classroom teaching, group work and occasional lectures, with company visits and an internship fair. The programme address is Prinsens Alle 2, 8800 Viborg. Students have 24/7 campus access. International counsellors answer admissions, programme and student-life questions and offer housing guidance; Dania owns no accommodation. Camp Logos is across the street and applications should be made after acceptance. Orientation precedes study start.

claim: A full IB Diploma qualifies for general access; qualifying Course Results give access to Danish AP and professional bachelor programmes, including this programme type.
excerpt: Structured restatement: An IB Diploma of at least 24 points gives general access subject to specific requirements. Course Results of at least 18 points, with grade 3 or better in all six subjects and at least three HL subjects, give access through quotas 1 and 2 to academy-profession and professional bachelor programmes. The university-bachelor supplementation rule is separate and does not apply to this professional bachelor.

claim: Dania holds positive institutional accreditation through 12 March 2032.
excerpt: Structured restatement of the extension letter dated 18 December 2025 on PDF page 1: Dania received positive institutional accreditations on 21 June 2018 and 12 March 2024; the latter accreditation was extended by two years through 12 March 2032. This is institutional accreditation, not a claim of a separate programme accreditation decision.

claim: The Danish counterpart names the professional bachelor award and explicitly opens applications on 1 February 2027.
excerpt: Structured restatement: The Danish page names Professionsbachelor i Cybersikkerhed, 195 ECTS and 3¼ years, and states applications open 1 February 2027 for September 2027 start. It labels its own teaching language Danish; the separately linked English programme page explicitly labels its international offering English.
interpretation: The local-language award page supports the Danish award title and opening date. Language of the English Opportunity is supported by the English full-degree catalogue and English programme page, not by the Danish-language counterpart.
